description: tri-ad, a passionate group that combines science, design, and technology for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Together, we are building HYDRA, an interactive space health and astronaut training concept designed to make space exploration safer and more engaging. We are excited to collaborate, innovate, and bring fresh creative energy to solving real challenges in human spaceflight
summary: HYDRA was made by team Triade from Riyadh for the NASA Space Apps Challenge because we wanted to tackle a real problem: with everyone's screen time going up lately, attention spans are shrinking, and when astronauts head into deep space, signals get delayed so they can't rely on real-time help from Earth. To fix this, we deliberately combined two separate challenges building a junior astronaut mission trainer and creating health monitoring software into one single platform. We did this because having a clutter of separate gadgets and tools, where each item has only one specific function, creates a massive mess and wastes critical time when you need to prepare for an emergency. By combining everything into one app, our long term vision is to open the door for every necessity to live in a single application accessible to everyone. This way, adult astronauts can quickly brush up on their facts and memories of what to do during intense emergency scenarios, while junior astronauts can learn about them and memorize how to handle these situations
details:
HYDRA is an all-in-one interactive training and mission support platform that pairs a biometric smart bracelet with gamified emergency simulations. It tracks live health and radiation metrics while training users through branching crisis scenarios, daily puzzle challenges, and an endless mode with multiple difficulty levels to keep knowledge sharp.

Operational Mechanics

The app connects to a biometric smart bracelet designed so you never have to take it off to charge, which monitors vitals like heart rate, SpO2, and core body temp alongside radiation levels. In the software, users choose between online and offline mission modes. The game engine processes player choices and reaction times against official NASA procedures, driving streak points and global rankings to keep users engaged daily.

Core Advantages and Value

It eliminates gadget clutter by merging health tracking and mission training into one device. It helps users build instant muscle memory and decision-making instincts for emergencies, gives adult astronauts a fast way to review protocols, gives junior astronauts an engaging way to learn, and provides a continuous safety net that works completely offline during deep space communication blackouts.

Long Term Vision and Goals

The project aims to solve deep space communication delay challenges and modern attention deficits. Long term, it supports Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 by advancing local STEM talent and spaceflight readiness, with future plans to scale into high risk terrestrial industries like commercial mining and deep sea diving using a centralized manager mode dashboard.

Development Stack and Technical Resources

Software and Design

Figma for UI and UX prototyping and interactive app wireframes, Canva for the seven slide pitch deck layout, and Procreate for hand drawn two dimensional bracelet concept art and visual sketches.

AI Assistance

Claude used for auxiliary UI code support and logic structuring.

Hardware Concepts and Data Models

Spatial telemetry data models, PPG sensors, micro thermistor, dosimeter, and piezoelectric kinetic battery concepts.

Core NASA Resources

NASA Spaceflight Human System Standard Volume 1 Crew Health, Space Mission Human Reliability Analysis Project, and the Emergency Procedures Handbook.
